comparator.name: Bachelor Taal- en Cultuurstudies
comparator.route: Taal en communicatie; Cultuur, communicatie en diversiteit; Communicatie, organisatie en interactie
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026-27 programme-specific EER defines Taal- en Cultuurstudies as a broad 180-EC humanities bachelor. The required structure is 15 EC of thematic orientation courses, 15 EC of language/culture/history courses, 7.5 EC of Theory and Practice of the Humanities, a major direction of at least 90 EC, a compulsory stage or study-abroad element of at least 7.5 EC, and remaining student-chosen space sufficient to reach 180 EC. The major direction contains 15 EC of disciplinary and methodological preparation, one 30-EC core package, a non-overlapping 30-EC second coherent package, 7.5 EC of thesis preparation and a thesis of at least 7.5 EC; at least 37.5 EC of the direction must be level 3. The generic normalized target names no major direction. Taal en communicatie is selected because it most directly represents the programme's combined language-and-culture identity while remaining cross-cultural and societally oriented; the current official direction description explicitly covers language in use, organisational/public communication and cultural and linguistic differences. Its two current official packages, Cultuur, communicatie en diversiteit and Communicatie, organisatie en interactie, are combined as the required non-overlapping 30-EC core and second package. For the first-year restricted choices, the first-listed current options are used neutrally: Historische en eigentijdse verbeeldingen van identiteit and Feit en fictie. The Dutch-language TCG option is instantiated generically as the formally required literature plus linguistics/language-use pair because the EER defines their status and credits but does not require one unique named pair. Methods and Statistics 1 is selected from the formal preparatory list as the current methods course supporting the chosen direction; the second preparation component remains the route's discipline-specific preparation. A 7.5-EC stage is selected to satisfy the compulsory practical/international element, leaving 45 EC of genuine free choice to reach 180 EC. These decisions were fixed before UCR fit was considered.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum is organised by film and media study, communication, media history, digital culture and transnational cultural analysis; the label directly reflects those dominant strands.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: The comparator explicitly offers Film and Television Studies and New Media and Digital Culture as separate formal directions. Relative to the broad closest match, this completed route replaces a substantial history/philosophy/sociology cluster with a denser film, media, communication and transnational-culture sequence, changing at least 30 EC and materially shifting its academic priorities toward media systems and digital culture.

comparatorRouteSelection.route: Taal en communicatie; Cultuur, communicatie en diversiteit; Communicatie, organisatie en interactie
comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic target requires one of fourteen major directions. Taal en communicatie most directly represents the title's combined language-and-culture identity without narrowing the comparator to one historical period, artistic medium, religion or particular foreign language. Its two current packages jointly span intercultural diversity and communication within and from organisations, so they are selected as the required core and non-overlapping second package. This route was fixed independently of UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme’s broad generator evidence about understanding society through language and culture, combining arts/culture/social questions, connecting humanities disciplines and culture in public debate (16205, 16206, 16214, 16215). The remaining generator-eligible rows were assessed as six coherent official-direction clusters. Media, Communication and Digital Culture (16211, 16219, 16225, 16232) and Postcolonial, Gender and Cultural Power (16208, 16221, 16222, 16223, 16234) are included because each is directly evidenced, coherent, materially distinct and feasible. Four further coherent clusters—language/communication/multilingualism; philosophy/politics/international history; arts/literature/historical cultures; and religion/culture—are recorded but cannot be included after the maximum of three alternatives is reached. The three completed schedules are pairwise distinct by at least four courses (30 EC), contain exactly 24 courses/180 EC, satisfy prerequisites and semester availability, and include at least six level-300 courses.

notes.text: Taal- en Cultuurstudies combines individually selected thematic and language/culture/history courses with one approved 90-EC major direction, a compulsory stage or study-abroad element and substantial free choice. UCR instead uses 24 fixed 7.5-EC courses across a liberal-arts curriculum. The comparison instantiates one valid TCS direction and preserves the 45-EC genuinely open space rather than pretending that every TCS student follows the same named courses.

The selected comparator pathway includes a credited route-specific thesis preparation, bachelor thesis and compulsory stage or study-abroad element. UCR offers optional independent research for comparison purposes, but no scheduled UCR course is a thesis or internship; those differences remain explicit.
